title: Gradle Lifecycle and the Task DAG Check

questions.prompt: Which approach best applies gradle lifecycle and the task dag?
options: Register cheap task models during configuration and express required order through data or task dependencies.
Run file generation at the top of build.gradle.kts
Assume task declaration order controls execution
Resolve every configuration before graph creation
questions.answer: Register cheap task models during configuration and express required order through data or task dependencies.
questions.explanation: The correct approach preserves Gradle’s lazy model, explicit data flow, variant correctness, functional evidence and operability.

questions.prompt: Gradle executes every registered task after configuration.
questions.explanation: Calling an expensive function while configuring a registered task still performs that work during configuration; placing text inside the registration block does not make it an execution action.

questions.answer: The requested tasks and the directed dependency graph Gradle constructs for that invocation.
questions.explanation: The answer names the model property that makes the build behaviour predictable rather than relying on incidental script order.
